paraphrase: Sages led by Śaunaka at Brahmāvarta, under a great banyan, ask Mārkaṇḍeya how he lives long in bliss; he: by the secret knowledge of Śiva (Śiva-tattva).

checks.note: The prose frame before v. 1 is located: sages led by Śaunaka at Brahmāvarta, under the great bhāṇḍīra banyan, ask Mārkaṇḍeya; he answers 'paramarahasyaśivatattvajñānena'.

paraphrase: The deity is Dakṣiṇāmūrti; his mantras are given with meditation forms — the teacher seated under the banyan, showing the gesture of knowledge in silence.

checks.note: E-text vv. 1-3 give the 24-syllable mantra and its dhyāna (sphaṭikarajatavarṇaṃ … dakṣiṇāmūrtim īḍe). Further mantras and dhyānas continue to v. 14.

paraphrase: The lamp of knowledge burns with the oil of dispassion and the wick of devotion; 'dakṣiṇā' means understanding (śemuṣī), and he who faces it is Dakṣiṇāmūrti; by this knowledge Brahmā gained power to create.

checks.note: The e-text numbers the mantra and meditation verses 1-14. The lamp of knowledge (vairāgyatailasampūrṇe bhaktivartisamanvite … jñaptidīpam) is v. 15. 'śemuṣī dakṣiṇā proktā' is v. 19. Brahmā gaining the power to create (sargasāmarthyam āpya) is v. 20. E-text vv. 4-6 are mantra-formation verses.
